messages:
anya: Heads up — we got a support ticket where a customer sends mixed-dim embeddings (256 + 1536) in one request and gets 413s. They expect partial success. Can we decide API semantics?

sam: Do we have a repro? paste of client payload?

anya: repro attached in the ticket, small/large vectors in one items array. Server rejects with 413: 
```
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "batch too large (byte limit 5MB)",
  "hint": "split by size or dims"
}
```

miguel: Our splitter currently assumes homogeneous dims per batch. Mixed dims hit the routing layer which does a best-effort fallback -> triggers size calc mismatch and we surface 413.

kevin: Two options: 1) enforce homogeneous-dim per request (quick, clear error + doc change) 2) accept heterogeneous but do internal split & return per-item statuses (partial success). Tradeoffs: latency, cost, billing clarity.

tara: UX note — console customers will be confused if some items succeed and some fail without clear per-item telemetry. If we do partial success we must expose per-item IDs & status in the response and surfaced in the Console call log.

sam: Implementation detail: If we split server-side we need a stable header to indicate original batch layout for reassembly and billing. Propose `X-Embed-Batch-Map: 0,1,2->0;3->1` (or a compact index map).

miguel: Also need to tag telemetry: `embed.size_bucket` (small/medium/large) + `embed.split_source: server` so we can measure split rate and CPU cost.

kevin: Quotas: current per-route token/byte quotas assume whole-request accounting. If we split server-side we should bill by item accepted bytes, not original request bytes. Ops impact: quota enforcement must be routed to split shards.

anya: Customers prefer no-fail behavior. But we must avoid silently masking malformed requests. Suggest: default to strict (error) for now, add an opt-in header `X-Embed-Accept-Partial: true` for partial success, then iterate. That allows a controlled rollout.

sam: +1. Plan: land server-side splitter behind feature flag `embed.partial_accept_v1`, and accept `X-Embed-Accept-Partial`. Response shape: 
```json
{
  "accepted": [ {"index":0, "id":"abc", "len":1536}, {"index":2, "id":"def", "len":256} ],
  "rejected": [ {"index":1, "reason":"dim_mismatch"} ]
}
```
(we'll include request_id and billing tokens)

miguel: We need to be careful with KV cache reuse: different dims -> different model variants. We must avoid cross-contamination. Splitter should route to model variant by dim header. Add header: `X-Embed-Dim: 256` per sub-request when we issue internal calls.

kevin: Console changes: add a per-route histogram of input dims (0-512, 513-1024, 1025-2048), show split-rate, and indicate per-size quota consumption. Also add a diagnostic link to raw request bodies (obfuscated) for support.

tara: Telemetry retention: we should keep per-dim histograms for 30 days and per-route split rates for 7 days. We should also emit a short log: `embed.split event` with fields: route, src_dim, num_items, bytes.

anya: Rollout plan: dev -> staging (dark traffic with 5% of embed traffic mirrored) -> canary (2% live with header opt-in) -> general. We'll gate by no increase in p99 latency > 5ms and split error rate < 0.5%.

sam: PR checklist: server splitter + feature-flag, response contract, unit tests for partial reassembly, telemetry events, e2e with billing mock.

miguel: Ops: need routing rule change to route by `X-Embed-Dim` when present, otherwise continue to reject mixed dims. Also update quota enforcement to operate at sub-request granularity behind the flag.

kevin: One more API debate: should we introduce a top-level schema change to the embeddings request that allows explicit per-item dims to avoid the server guessing? Eg: `items: [{id, vector, dims:1536}, ...]`. Pros: explicit, simpler server logic. Cons: breaks current clients. Could be an opt-in schema version header `X-Embed-Version: 2`.

anya: Good call. Add `X-Embed-Version: 2` as future follow-up. For now stick to `X-Embed-Accept-Partial` + flag.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/embed-splitter v2 -> 2023-07-21 02:45 UTC (dry-run).

tara: Follow-ups: update Console call-log UX copy, add a small tooltip explaining partial acceptance, and create a support playbook. I'll own the UX copy.

anya: OK — owners: sam (implementation), miguel (routing + infra), kevin (console + quota), tara (UX + support doc). I'll write the RFC and link it to the ticket: https://redwood.internal/r/embeds/splitter-2023

sam: I'll open the PR today and tag @kevin @miguel for infra review.

kevin: :thumbsup:

anya: Thanks — keeping this thread for rollout notes.
